name: Dushanbe International Airport
before:
Tajikistan's main airport, in the capital Dushanbe, and the hub for Somon Air and the home base for Tajik Air.

The terminal is newer than the country's aviation reputation suggests. A French built terminal opened on 3 September 2014, rated for 1.5 million passengers a year, funded by a 20 million euro long term loan from France alongside 19 million euros from Tajikistan itself.

There is a single runway of 3,112 metres at an altitude of 785 metres, plus a dedicated helicopter stand for aircraft up to 12 tonnes.

The airport has one extraordinary moment in its history. On 7 September 1992, in the early months of the Tajikistani civil war, President Rahmon Nabiyev was ambushed on his way here by opposition forces and then forced to resign at gunpoint in the terminal's VIP lounge, with tanks and troops stationed outside, before being released.
after:
The airport for the Tajik capital, Dushanbe, is the hub for Somon Air and the home base for Tajik Air.

There is a single runway of about 3,100 metres at an altitude of 785 metres.

claims.note: Tajik Air's own site (© 2026) says it flies from Dushanbe and gives a Dushanbe address; Khovar (29 Jan 2026) reports the national carrier settled its leasing debt in 2025 and plans to lease two Airbus aircraft. Neither OurAirports nor the Wikipedia article links tajikair.tj, so it was checked against Khovar: both name the same director general (Parviz Shodmonzoda) and the same settled leasing dispute. Its flights are now all domestic (see the held-back note below).

claims.wasBefore: On 7 September 1992, in the early months of the Tajikistani civil war, President Rahmon Nabiyev was ambushed on his way here by opposition forces and then forced to resign at gunpoint in the terminal's VIP lounge, with tanks and troops stationed outside, before being released.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The New York Times report it cites (8 Sep 1992) is blocked by the session's egress policy (not retried by any other route), and Asia-Plus's own archive for 7 Sep 2022, the 30th anniversary, has no piece on it. Two attempts; no second source reached.

Held back: verified but replaces nothing (the old text gave no passenger figure, only the 2014 terminal's rated capacity, which is cut). Khovar (28 Jan 2026), reporting the Civil Aviation Agency's press conference: more than 2,160,000 passengers in 2025 (1,060,746 arriving and 1,099,502 departing, which adds up to 2,160,248); Wikipedia's infobox gives 2,160,248 for 2025. For Andy to add if he wants.

claims.claim: no Dushanbe to London flight for now
claims.why: Held back: new, and on one source. Asia-Plus (28 Jan 2026) reports the head of Tajikistan's Civil Aviation Agency saying the planned Dushanbe to London route will not launch for now because it would not pay; only three tickets were sold on the version via Tbilisi. Relevant to UK agents, so named for Andy; it would need the agency's own statement or a second report to go in.

claims.claim: Tajik Air now flies only within Tajikistan
claims.why: Held back: new detail. Tajik Air's own site says it flies from Dushanbe to six towns in the country and grew from one aircraft to four in 2025 after settling old debts (Khovar, 29 Jan 2026, reports the debt settled and two Airbus aircraft planned on finance lease). An agent reading 'home base for Tajik Air' may assume international flights; Andy may want the text to say its flights are domestic.
